subject: Polity
description: Covers PAC, Estimates Committee, and DRSCs.

questions.stem: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC), one of the most important financial committees of Parliament, is primarily tasked with examining the audit reports submitted by:

options.option_text: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
The Finance Commission of India
The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) is the oldest parliamentary committee, set up in 1921. Its primary function is to examine the annual audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India, which are laid before Parliament by the President. The CAG acts as the "friend, philosopher, and guide" to the PAC, helping them expose financial irregularities and wasteful expenditure by the government.
DECOY BUSTING: The RBI manages monetary policy and banking, not government audits. The Finance Commission dictates tax devolution between Centre and States. The CVC is the apex anti-corruption body.
EXAM INSIGHT: By convention (since 1967), the Chairman of the PAC is always chosen from the Opposition party to ensure strict and unbiased scrutiny of the ruling government's expenses.

questions.stem: Which is the largest parliamentary committee in terms of membership, consisting exclusively of members from the Lok Sabha?

options.option_text: Estimates Committee
Public Accounts Committee (PAC)
Committee on Public Undertakings
Business Advisory Committee

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Estimates Committee is the largest committee of the Parliament, consisting of 30 members. Crucially, all 30 members are elected SOLELY from the Lok Sabha. There is no representation from the Rajya Sabha. Its job is to examine the budget estimates and suggest 'economies' in public expenditure (acting as a continuous economy committee).
DECOY BUSTING: Both the PAC and the Committee on Public Undertakings have 22 members each (15 from Lok Sabha and 7 from Rajya Sabha). 
EXAM INSIGHT: A minister cannot be elected as a member of any of these three financial committees. This ensures the committees remain independent watchdogs of the executive's financial actions.

questions.stem: The system of Departmentally-Related Standing Committees (DRSCs) was created in 1993 to ensure detailed scrutiny of government grants. Currently, how many such committees exist?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: There are currently 24 Departmentally-Related Standing Committees (DRSCs). Each committee consists of 31 members (21 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha). Out of the 24 committees, 8 work under the Rajya Sabha and 16 under the Lok Sabha.
DECOY BUSTING: The system started with 17 committees in 1993, which was expanded to 24 in 2004. 
EXAM INSIGHT: These committees are the unsung heroes of Parliament. When the budget is presented, Parliament goes into recess for a few weeks. During this recess, the 24 DRSCs meticulously analyze the detailed budget demands of individual ministries before Parliament reconvenes to vote on them.

questions.stem: Who chairs the Business Advisory Committee of the Lok Sabha, making it one of the few parliamentary committees with an ex-officio presiding head?

options.option_text: Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha, the committee's deputy convener
Speaker of Lok Sabha, who serves as its ex-officio chairperson
Prime Minister of India, as the leader of government business
Minister of Parliamentary Affairs, who coordinates House scheduling

questions.explanation: The Speaker of Lok Sabha chairs the Business Advisory Committee as an ex-officio head — this is explicitly provided in Lok Sabha Rules. The Committee recommends the time to be allotted for the transaction of government business. The Deputy Speaker is not its chair; the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs coordinates logistics but does not preside over it.

questions.stem: When time allotted for discussing demands for grants expires in Lok Sabha, the Speaker applies the 'guillotine'. What does this procedure entail?

options.option_text: All undiscussed demands are put to vote and passed without debate
The sitting is adjourned and unfinished demands are deferred to next sitting
Undiscussed demands are returned to the concerned ministry for revision
The House refers all pending demands to the Estimates Committee for review

questions.explanation: Guillotine means bunching together all undiscussed demands for grants and voting on them en bloc without any debate when the allotted time expires. It is a procedural device to ensure the budget is passed in time. It does NOT lead to adjournment or referral — demands are effectively passed without scrutiny, which is why the Estimates Committee's pre-budget role is considered so important.

questions.stem: Which Parliamentary Committee is specifically tasked with examining whether rule-making powers delegated by Parliament to the executive are exercised within the intended scope and limits of the parent legislation?

options.option_text: Committee on Subordinate Legislation, scrutinising delegated rule-making
Public Accounts Committee, reviewing how the executive spends public funds
Committee on Privileges, safeguarding parliamentary rights and dignity
Committee on Government Assurances, tracking ministerial commitments made

questions.explanation: The Committee on Subordinate Legislation examines statutory rules, regulations, bye-laws, and notifications made by the executive under powers delegated by Parliament, to ensure they do not exceed the scope granted. Both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha have separate such committees. The PAC examines financial irregularities post-facto, not the exercise of delegated legislative powers.

questions.stem: Upon prorogation of the Lok Sabha, which of the following parliamentary committees does NOT lapse, continuing its work into the next session?

options.option_text: Select Committee constituted to examine a specific pending housing bill
Joint Committee formed to scrutinise a specific financial legislation
Ad hoc Committee set up to inquire into a specific public matter only
Standing Committee on Finance, a departmentally-related permanent body

questions.explanation: Departmentally Related Standing Committees (DRSCs) are permanent bodies and do not lapse on prorogation — they continue across sessions. Ad hoc committees (Select Committees and Joint Committees on specific bills) lapse on prorogation of the House. Students often confuse Standing Committees with Select Committees; the former are permanent, the latter are bill-specific and transient.

questions.stem: The Committee on Government Assurances monitors which specific category of ministerial statements made on the floor of Parliament?

options.option_text: Assurances, promises, and undertakings given by ministers during debates
Policy statements issued by ministers on national security and defence
Budget speeches and fiscal proposals presented by the Finance Minister
Explanations offered by ministers in response to the Presidential address

questions.explanation: This committee scrutinises assurances, promises, and undertakings given by ministers during debates, Question Hour, or other proceedings, and reports on the extent to which they have been implemented. It does not examine policy statements, budget proposals, or Presidential Address replies. Both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha have separate Committees on Government Assurances.

questions.stem: Under the Indian Constitution, which category of bill is constitutionally barred from being referred to a Joint Committee of both Houses of Parliament for examination?

options.option_text: Ordinary bills already passed by one House and pending in the other House
Money Bills, which follow a special procedure under Article 109 of the Constitution
Constitution Amendment Bills requiring special majority in both Houses separately
Bills on State List subjects introduced with prior Presidential recommendation

questions.explanation: Article 109 of the Constitution lays down a special procedure for Money Bills — they can only originate in Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha's role is limited to recommendations within 14 days. Referring a Money Bill to a Joint Committee is constitutionally impermissible because it would give Rajya Sabha equal standing on a Money Bill, contrary to Article 109. Constitution Amendment Bills and ordinary bills can be referred to Joint Committees; Option C is a common distractor because students associate special majority with restricted procedure.

questions.stem: The Estimates Committee is called a 'continuous economy committee' while the PAC is called a 'post-mortem committee'. Which statement most precisely captures this functional distinction?

options.option_text: Estimates Committee examines future budget proposals before grants are voted by Parliament
PAC covers only capital expenditure; Estimates Committee covers only revenue expenditure
Estimates Committee draws members from both Houses; PAC has only Lok Sabha members
PAC is chaired by an Opposition member; Estimates is chaired by the Finance Minister

questions.explanation: The Estimates Committee looks forward — it examines demands for grants before they are voted and suggests economies or alternative policies. PAC looks backward — it examines CAG audit reports on past expenditure. Option B is wrong: PAC examines all categories of expenditure, not only capital. Option C reverses the reality: it is PAC (not Estimates Committee) that has members from both Houses (15 from Lok Sabha + 7 from Rajya Sabha); Estimates Committee has 30 members all from Lok Sabha. Option D's second half is wrong: the Estimates Committee is chaired by an elected member of the ruling party, NOT the Finance Minister.
